Q: Mounted directory empty with Docker Compose and custom Dockerfile A:

EDIT: So, I was able to get this to work... although, it slightly more difficult than just specifying a path..

You can accomplish this by specifying a volume in docker-compose.yml.. The path to the directory (on the host) is labeled as device in the compose file.. It appears that the root of the path has to be an actual volume (possibly a share would work) but the 'destination' of the path can be a directory on the specified volume..

I created a new volume called docker on my machine but I suppose you could do this with your existing disk/volume..

I am on a Mac and this docker-compose.yml file worked for me:

version: '3.7'
services:
  nodemon-test:
    container_name: my-nodemon-test
    image: oze4/nodemon-docker-test
    ports:
      - "1337:1337"
    volumes:
      - docker_test_app:/app    # see comment below on which name to use here

volumes:
  docker_test_app:              # use this name under `volumes:` for the service
    name: docker_test_app
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
       o: bind
       type: none
       device: /Volumes/docker/docker_test_app

The container specified exists in my DockerHub.. this is the source code for it, just in case you are worried about anything malicious. I created it like two weeks ago to help someone else on StackOverflow.

Shows files from the container on my machine (the host)..

You can read more about Docker Volume configs here if you would like.

ORIGINAL ANSWER:

It looks like you are trying to share the build directory with your host machine.. After some testing, it appears Docker will overwrite the specified path on the container with the contents of the path on the host.

If you run docker logs my_laravel you should see an error about missing files at /var/www/site.. So, even though the build is successful - once Docker mounts the directory from your machine (./site) onto the container (/var/www/site) it overwrites the path within the container (/var/www/site) with the contents of the path on your host (./site) - which is empty.

To test and make sure the contents of /var/www/site are in fact being overwritten, you can run docker exec -it /bin/bash (you may need to replace /bin/bash with /bash).. This will give you command line access inside of the container. From there you can do ls -a /var/www/site..

Furthermore, you can also pre-stage ./site to have a random test file in it (test.txt or whatever), then docker-compose up -d, then run the same commands from the step above docker exec -it ... and see if the staged test.txt file is now inside the container - this gives you definitive evidence that when you run volumes, the data on your host overwrites data in the container.

With that being said, doing something like this and sharing a log directory will work... the volume path specified on the container is still overwritten, the difference is the container is writing to that path.. it doesn't rely on it for config files/app files.

Hope this helps.

Q: 'Failed to finalize LSBundleWrapper' on SwiftUI app build for release A:

In my case, I had moved my Xcode project (to an external drive as no space!), the DerivedData setting remained on the main drive in $HOME/Library/Development/Xcode/DerivedData. However it would not build (same error as above). Deleting the DerivedData project subdirectory and retrying, fixed it.

Q: MS Excel displays garbled characters for Azerbaijani text in CSV file exported with UTF-8 encoding A:

Setting the BOM should work. But have you tried Data > Get Data > From File (Text/CSV) menu to manually set the encoding to 65001: UTF-8?

Q: Restrict access to Logic App to Managed Identity A:

Summary: Call the logic app from the App Service passing a token instead of a shared access signature (SAS). Then, validate the token in the logic app using a policy on the subject claim.

Steps:

  1. Delete the sp, sv and sig query parameters (this is the SAS) from the logic app URI.
// Original: "https://prod-nnn.region.logic.azure.com/workflows/877...394/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=2016-10-01&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=n6R...ffo"
string logicAppUri = "https://prod-nnn.region.logic.azure.com/workflows/877...394/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=2016-10-01";
  1. In the App Service code, get a token for any known resource and pass it to the logic app.
DefaultAzureCredential credential = new();
string anyPublicScope = "https://management.azure.com/.default";
AccessToken token = await credential.GetTokenAsync(new TokenRequestContext(new[] { anyPublicScope }));
httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new("Bearer", token.Token);

var input = new { LogicAppParam1 = 123, LogicAppParam2 = "cool" };
using StringContent content = new(JsonSerializer.Serialize(input), Encoding.UTF8, MediaTypeNames.Application.Json);
HttpResponseMessage response = await httpClient.PostAsync(logicAppUri, content);
  1. Find your tenant id and the id of your App Service managed identity. In Azure portal:
  • open Azure Active Directory and copy the value of Tenant ID from the Overview page.
  • open your App Service, go to Identity and copy the value of Object (principal) ID.
  1. In Azure portal open the logic app, go to Authorization and add a policy like that:
Policy name = Your App Service
Issuer = https://sts.windows.net/paste-tenant-id-here-and-add-a-slash/
Subject = paste-managed-identity-object-id-here

Add one policy for each App Service or User who must be able to trigger the logic app.

There is NO NEED to do any of the following things, although you will find many turotials which do them:

  • Create an App Registration for the logic app. Configure resource uri, scopes, consent options etc.

  • Add the Audience claim to the logic app policy.

    Update: Microsoft made the Audience claim required since April 2026.

  • Add "operationOptions": "IncludeAuthorizationHeadersInOutputs" to the logic app trigger, in code view.

  • Parse the token with logic app actions to decide who can do what.

  • List allowed inbound IP addresses to the logic app Workflow settings page.

More info:

  • The Issuer(iss) claim is required for creating a policy. You would have the same security without it (because the Subject claim is globally unique) but you just have to fill the Issuer correctly.

  • The Audience(aud) claim contains the uri or id of the requested resource. It is deducted from the scope passed to GetTokenAsync(). In this case it would be https://management.azure.com. This is an arbitratry public resource, not related to the logic app, so there is no point in validating the Audience claim in the logic app policy. Anyone in your Azure tenant could request a token for that resource but only your specific App Service can provide a Subject claim = the id of the managed identity.

    Update: Microsoft made the Audience claim required since April 2026. I used "https://management.azure.com" and it worked.

  • In case you want to allow a User (not an App Service) you have two options:

    • a) Use the Subject(sub) claim but it does not contain the user's AAD Object ID. It contains a unique hash of the user/application combination. Decode one user token to get the claim.
    • b) (haven't tried this) The oid claim always contains the AAD Object ID of the User or App Service. It cannot be selected from the list in policy editor but you could Add custom claim.

  • You cannot call a logic app with both a token and a SAS. You must remove the SAS, otherwise an error is returned. This is good - you should never store secrets in config files under version control.

  • When debugging in VS, DefaultAzureCredential gets a token for the current user so you must add a policy for a user sub (see caveat above).

  • When deployed to Azure, DefaultAzureCredential gets a token for the managed identity of the App Service.

  • There are shorter methods to send JSON with HttpClient like .PostAsJsonAsync(uri, input) and .PostAsync(uri, JsonContent.Create(input)) but after I added the Authorization header they stopped working - they sent an empty body. This is why I use the longer StringContent variant but you might be luckier.

Q: How to determine if a Selenium WebDriver is running in headless mode A:

navigator.plugins.length

navigator.plugins.length is a JavaScript property that returns the number of browser plugins (like Flash, PDF viewers) being installed and is accessed via the navigator object's plugins property, which yields a PluginArray. navigator.plugins.length is predominantly used for fingerprinting and content detection, often returning 0 or limited info.

navigator.webdriver

navigator.webdriver is a read-only browser property that indicates if the user-agent or the browser is controlled by automation software like Selenium.

So in short neither of the navigator properties would help in asserting headless mode.

Solution

To determine the Chrome Headless mode the most reliable method will be to assert the user-agent for the presence of the string Headless as follows:

Code block:

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

options = Options()
options.add_argument("--headless")
driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options)
# driver = webdriver.Chrome()
print(driver.execute_script("return navigator.userAgent;"))
try:
    assert "Headless" in driver.execute_script("return navigator.userAgent;")
    print("Headless mode invoked")
except:
    print("Headless mode not invoked")
driver.quit()

Console Output:

Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) HeadlessChrome/144.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
Headless mode invoked

References

You can find a detailed discussion in:

  • How to detect if Chrome browser is headless in selenium?
